name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before any human review. It catches 80% of trivia, freeing humans to focus on real design and trade-offs. The trade-off is setup time and occasional false positives, but those are tiny compared to the cost of missed details.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s false positives aren’t the only risk—it also misses context-dependent issues like architectural debt or subtle UX trade-offs that matter more than trivia. A better alternative is to gate PR-Agent on *specific* checks (e.g., linting, dependency bumps) while reserving human review for design and trade-offs. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: compare PR-Agent’s output to human reviews, measure missed critical issues vs. false positives, and decide based on real data.
